text: The purchaser will likely prevail because when he bought the house from the man, the recorded easement was revived as an appurtenant right that runs with the land. Although the merger doctrine extinguished the easement temporarily when the man owned both parcels, selling only the dominant estate (the house) automatically re-established the burden on the servient estate (the highway-side lot). Therefore, the man cannot block access to a path he previously granted and which is now legally enforceable against his remaining land. CONFIDENCE: 95
